OrchestrationTaskStatus.description: `failed` is final: the task's attempts ran out (or it failed in a way a retry cannot mend), and a person decides what happens to it. `blocked`: a task waiting behind one that failed, which is not the same as `pending`, waiting for its turn. `skipped`: that decision, giving the branch up so the graph can finish without it. `stopped` is someone's decision and is never retried on its own; `interrupted` is a task whose execution a wrapper restart cut off, which is: the chat goes on in a new execution, in the worktree it left, while attempts remain.

Health.description: The same verdict on anything that works: a chat, or an orchestration task.

ChatHealth.description: Whether a chat is working as it should, computed in core at the moment it is read (a command that has been running for too long is a fact of the clock, so a snapshot ages: readers of a live chat read it again). `level` is the worst of the `signals`, ordered worst first, and `reason` is the first one's; with no signal the chat is `ok` and `reason` says so.

level.description: Never `ok`: a signal that fired is a warning or a problem

reason.description: One line a person reads, with the figures that made it fire

since.description: When the condition started, for the signals that measure a stretch of time

detail.description: What made it fire, when the line is not enough: the command, the file, the figures

hint.description: Text the panel prefills the hint box with. Agentry writes it, not the model: a suggestion per signal is worth more than an empty box to someone who has just been told a worker is stuck.

toolUseId.description: The tool call to cancel, when the signal is about one command that is still running

HealthSignalKind.description:
What a signal noticed. Only what Agentry can tell from what it already receives is here: a command that runs far longer than it should, a chat that has gone quiet while it should be working, and facts of the chat itself (how its last execution ended, that it waits for a person, that its context is nearly full, that a branch failed).

The second group comes from docs/plans/agent-observability.md and is about a worker that is busy without getting anywhere: the same tool call over and over (`repeat-stall`), no commit and no file touched for a long stretch (`no-progress`), the same few steps in a cycle (`loop`), a test edited so that it stops asserting what it asserted (`weakened-test`), and the ceiling of  {@link  TaskLimits }  coming close (`budget`).

permissionPrompts.description: `host` sends permissions, questions and plans to the panel; `none`, the default, denies them

account.description: Pin it to a claude-swap account (slot number, email or alias) instead of the active one

ForkChatRequest.description: Continues a chat in a copy of it, which is a new chat that records where it came from.

ChatMessageRequest.description: A message to a chat that has a live execution.

ChatSettingsUpdate.description: What can be changed on a live execution without restarting it.

from.description: The days asked for, inclusive; null when unbounded

days.description: Oldest first, only days something was spent on

orchestrations.description: Most spent first; only the chats that work for an orchestration

UsageReport.description: What the chats spent, per day, per project and per orchestration.

costUsd.description: Sum of what the CLI reported; null when it reported nothing for any chat in it: read as "not available"

chatsWithoutCost.description: Chats in these totals whose cost the CLI never reported (started from a terminal), so `costUsd` leaves them out

UsageTotals.description: What was spent over some stretch of chats. Tokens are real and cover every chat; the cost only covers the chats that reported one.

costUsd.description: Sum of what the CLI reported; null when it reported nothing for any chat in it: read as "not available"

chatsWithoutCost.description: Chats in these totals whose cost the CLI never reported (started from a terminal), so `costUsd` leaves them out

costUsd.description: Sum of what the CLI reported; null when it reported nothing for any chat in it: read as "not available"

chatsWithoutCost.description: Chats in these totals whose cost the CLI never reported (started from a terminal), so `costUsd` leaves them out

project.description: Null for the chats under no imported project

costUsd.description: Sum of what the CLI reported; null when it reported nothing for any chat in it: read as "not available"

chatsWithoutCost.description: Chats in these totals whose cost the CLI never reported (started from a terminal), so `costUsd` leaves them out

TaskHintRequest.description: A nudge sent to a task that is still running, from the orchestration board.

HintRequest.description: A nudge sent to something that is still running, without typing into its conversation: the text reaches the worker as its next user message.

id.description: Ours: not derived from the path or from anything the CLI writes

exists.description: The directory is still on disk

chatCount.description: Chats under the project and its worktrees

Project.description: A directory the person imported, with the worktrees that belong to it.

createdBy.description: The orchestration task that created it, when one did

ProjectWorktree.description: A git worktree of a project.

ProjectCandidate.description: A directory chats have run in that is not imported, offered on first start.

ImportProjectRequest.description: Imports a directory; every chat under it is adopted, retroactively.

branch.description: Null when the worktree is on a detached head

base.description: What `branch` is compared against: the commit the worktree branched from

ahead.description: Commits on `branch` that `base` does not have

uncommitted.description: Working-tree changes that are in no commit, staged or not

ChangeSummary.description: What a branch has done: the work it committed, and what it has not committed yet.

FileDiff.description: One file's diff, unified, exactly as git prints it: the panel highlights it, nobody parses it.

summary.description: Null when the chat's directory is not a git checkout

touched.description: What the chat's `Write`/`Edit`/`NotebookEdit` calls touched, newest first

ChatChanges.description: What a chat changed. A chat in a git checkout has a `summary`; one working somewhere else has none, and then the transcript is the only honest record of what it wrote.

at.description: When the tool call that touched it ran

TouchedFile.description: A file a chat wrote where git cannot answer, read from the chat's own transcript.

updatedAt.description: When the worker last rewrote it; null when it never wrote one

Checklist.description: A worker's plan for itself, as of its last update.

ChecklistItem.description: One item of a worker's own checklist, from its `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`TodoWrite` calls.

diffCommand.description: Command for a side-by-side diff, e.g. `code --diff {left} {right}`; no button when absent

pathMap.description: Container paths rewritten to host paths before the template is filled; first match wins

EditorSettings.description: How the panel turns a path and a line into something that opens the person's editor. It is a setting because the wrapper often runs in a container while the editor does not, and because nobody agrees on an editor: `vscode://file/{path}:{line}` is only the default.

reason.description: Shown to the worker in the failed tool result, so it knows a person stopped it and why

CancelCommandRequest.description: Kills one command's process tree without ending the turn: the descendants of the CLI process that belong to that tool call, found by pid, never by matching a command line. The worker gets a failed tool result and carries on. Which call is in the path.

engineReason.description: Why the planner chose the engine, shown next to it in the draft

synthesize.description: Launch a final agent that synthesizes the results

worktree.description: Give every task its own git worktree and branch, so parallel workers never write over each other — and never edit the checkout the wrapper itself is running from.

maxAttempts.description: Attempts a failed task gets in total, the first included, before a person has to decide (default 2)

allowedTools.description: Tools every worker may use without being asked. A worker has no one to ask unless `permissionPrompts` sends its prompts to the panel, so anything it needs beyond editing files has to be pre-authorised here or approved there.

permissionPrompts.description: `host` routes each worker's permission prompts to the panel for a person to answer

limits.description: Default ceiling for every task that does not set its own

verification.description: Checks to run on the integration branch once the graph is merged; none when absent

RelaunchOrchestrationRequest.description: Runs a finished graph again with corrections, as a new orchestration that records where it came from. What is left out keeps the original's value; `tasks` replaces the whole list, because merging two graphs by task id is guesswork nobody asked for.

OrchestrationTemplate.description: A graph saved to be run again on another objective. Settings-shaped, so a JSON file.

name.description: Name of the orchestration; the template's when absent

LaunchOrchestrationTemplateRequest.description: Launches a template. What is given here overrides the template's spec for this run only.

tokenSet.description: A token has been set, which is all a reader may know about it

readOnly.description: Reject every mutating method with 405, except answering a permission prompt

AuthConfig.description: How the API is guarded. The token is **never** in this document: only its hash is stored, and the token itself is shown once, when it is set. `token?: never` says so in the type, so no route can leak it by echoing the configuration back.

AuthMode.description: `none` is the default and is what a local install has always done. `token` is a bearer token, accepted as a query parameter only on `GET /api/events`, which `EventSource` cannot set headers on. `oidc` validates a JWT against the issuer's JWKS.

SetAuthTokenRequest.description: Sets or rotates the bearer token. Omit it to have Agentry generate one.

AuthTokenResult.description: The only time the token is ever returned.

actor.description: Token id or OIDC subject; `local` when no authentication is configured

summary.description: One line about what it did, built from the route, not from the payload

AuditEntry.description: One mutating request. Never the body: prompts and secrets live there.

total.description: Entries matching the filter, so a caller knows what is left below `from`

from.description: Offset of the first entry within the filtered set

id.description: The MCP server's name, which is how the CLI knows it

scopes.description: What it was granted, when the CLI reports it

ConnectorStatus.description: `unknown`: the CLI lists the server but says nothing about its session.

ConnectorAction.description: A button that opens a new chat with a prompt already written. Nothing more magic than that.

number.description: Slot number, the same identifier  {@link  AccountSummary }  uses

configDir.description: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for every process started for this account. Null shares the wrapper's, which is what every account did before and stays the default: moving someone's `~/.claude` without being asked is not something a wrapper gets to do.

AccountConfig.description: Agentry's own settings for one claude-swap slot: what the binary itself does not keep.

threshold.description: Utilization (0-100) of the active account past which the next one is taken

order.description: Slot numbers to try, in order; every enabled account when absent

projects.description: Project ids this policy governs; the account's default policy when absent

RotationPolicy.description: Which accounts a project may use, in what order, and when to move on.

configDir.description: Null goes back to sharing the wrapper's config dir

rotationPolicy.description: Null removes the policy, leaving the global auto-switch in charge

pct.description: Share of the window consumed (0-100), exactly as claude-swap reported it

UsageHistoryPoint.description: One reading of an account's usage, kept as a row so the panel can draw a line.

UsageWindowKind.description: Which rate-limit window a usage point belongs to.

cron.description: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week

timezone.description: IANA zone the expression is read in; the server's when absent

lastRunAt.description: Null until it has fired once

nextRunAt.description: Null when it is disabled, or when the expression will never fire again

Schedule.description: A recurring chat or orchestration. The definition is settings-shaped, so it lives in a JSON file; the runs accumulate, so they are rows. A window missed while the wrapper was down is skipped, not replayed: firing a week of cron slots at once on boot is never what anyone meant.

ScheduleTarget.description: What a schedule starts when it fires.

ScheduleRunStatus.description: `started`: it launched, and what happened next belongs to the chat or the orchestration. `skipped`: the slot passed while the wrapper was down.

enabled.description: Starts enabled unless this says otherwise

timezone.description: Null goes back to the server's zone

points.description: Oldest first, one point per bucket of the range, empty ones included so a chart has no gaps

UsageSeries.description: Cost and usage over time, for a chart.

UsageBucket.description: How wide one point of a usage series is.

at.description: Start of the bucket, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the server's time zone

costUsd.description: Null when no chat in the bucket reported a cost; never estimated from a price table

UsageBreakdown.description: The same range cut two ways. Most spent first in both.

label.description: What to show: the project's name, or the model id as the CLI writes it

UsageSlice.description: What one project or one model spent over a range.

ExportFormat.description: How a transcript is exported: Markdown for a person, JSON faithful to the events.

current.description: The CLI on the PATH, as it reports itself; null when it is not installed

pinned.description: The version the image pins, when it pins one

latest.description: Newest published version; null when the check has never run or could not reach the registry

updateAvailable.description: `latest` is newer than `current`; false whenever either of them is unknown

error.description: Why the last check failed (registry unreachable, unexpected answer); the previous `latest` is kept

CliVersionInfo.description: Which Claude Code the wrapper runs and whether a newer one exists. The check costs a registry read, so it happens on demand or once a day, never on a page load: `checkedAt` says how old the answer is.
